notes: p053 starts a new indented paragraph after p052 ended with «يَا رَحْمَنُ.», so there is no + marker; p052's footnotes end on that page, so there is no (تابع). p054 and p056 continue sentences from the previous page (+). There are no footnotes, headings or bold on pp.053-056: the whole dua is set in one heavier font. p053: the kasra under «الله» in «بِسْمِ اللهِ» sits low between the lines but belongs to line 1, and «بِاللهِ» also has a printed kasra. Following my earlier batches, Allah is written with only the printed case vowel (the automatic ligature shadda/small alif is not written). p053: the print has no space after the comma in «يَخْتَلِفُون،اهْدِنِي»; I wrote one space under the one-space-between-words rule. Final ى in إِلَى/عَلَى/وَالنَّوَى/وَتَرْضَى has the automatic Lotus small alif, so it is written as plain ى. Partial vowelling is kept as printed, for example: نَعَّار، (no vowel on the ra'), الوَهَّاب., يَخْتَلِفُون، (no fatha on the nun), شيءٍ (p053, no fatha on the shin) against شَيء، and شَيءٌ (p054), عَيْن، (p054), أَصْلِح (kasra only on the lam), تَعْلَم، (twice), وَعَلَيكَ (first occurrence on p056, no sukun on the ya'), بَيْن يَدَيَّ, اجْعَل لِّي, وَأَعْظِم. Sukun printed on a madd ya' or waw is kept: وَإِسْرَافِيْلَ, فِيْمَا, خَطِيْئَتِي, دُوْنَكَ. Shadda is written before its vowel throughout.
